studies.title: Essentially Non-Oscillatory and Weighted Essentially Non-Oscillatory Schemes for Hyperbolic Conservation Laws
studies.weno_family_orders: ENO/WENO tutorial and lineage; multiple orders
studies.equations_dimensions_grid: hyperbolic conservation laws; scalar and systems; structured multidimensional discussion
studies.state_semantics: FD point values versus FV cell averages are distinguished
studies.reconstruction_flux: tutorial treatment; no single frozen head-to-head flux contract
studies.implementation: archival lecture/report; no released matched modern code pair
studies.hardware_precision: historical CPU context; precision not a comparison variable
studies.comparison_basis: algorithmic operation-count discussion rather than accuracy-normalized experiment
studies.reported_result: The multidimensional FD formulation is described as substantially cheaper in operation count than same-order FV because FV requires transverse reconstruction and quadrature.
studies.limitations: Operation counts are not measured end-to-end accelerator results and do not establish universal superiority.

studies.title: High-Order Finite Difference and Finite Volume WENO Schemes and Discontinuous Galerkin Methods for CFD
studies.equations_dimensions_grid: CFD conservation laws; structured-grid FD and FV plus DG
studies.reconstruction_flux: multiple representative schemes; not one identical numerical flux
studies.time_integration: multiple; not controlled as a single experiment
studies.implementation: comparative review with numerical examples and cost discussion
studies.hardware_precision: historical CPU; incomplete for modern reproducibility
studies.comparison_basis: accuracy, resolution, and computational cost across method classes
studies.reported_result: Direct comparative literature predates GradFlow; costs and capabilities are conditional on formulation and problem.
studies.limitations: A review-era comparison, not a modern matched GPU or differentiable study.

studies.title: High Order WENO and DG Methods for Time-Dependent Convection-Dominated PDEs: A Brief Survey of Several Recent Developments
studies.equations_dimensions_grid: convection-dominated PDEs; one and multiple dimensions; structured, curvilinear, and unstructured context
studies.state_semantics: explicitly distinguishes FD point values from FV cell averages
studies.comparison_basis: mathematical structure, implementation cost, and applicability
studies.method_specific_optimizations: distinguishes dimension-by-dimension and genuinely multidimensional FV costs
studies.reported_result: In one dimension FD and FV can have nearly identical code and cost; multidimensional FV reconstruction/quadrature is generally more costly, while FV is attractive for nonsmooth or unstructured geometry.
studies.limitations: Survey conclusions do not supply a modern accuracy-to-time CPU/GPU matrix.

studies.title: Observations on the Fifth-Order WENO Method with Non-Uniform Meshes
taxonomy_endpoints: finite-volume reconstruction on uniform and nonuniform meshes
studies.equations_dimensions_grid: one-dimensional tests; uniform and nonuniform/adaptive meshes; multidimensional costs discussed from prior work
studies.state_semantics: FD point values versus FV cell averages
studies.reconstruction_flux: fixed uniform linear reconstruction equivalence is analyzed; nonlinear WENO remains distinct
studies.hardware_precision: historical CPU; precision/hardware details insufficient for reproduction of current performance
studies.comparison_basis: accuracy and work on uniform/nonuniform grids
studies.execution_boundary: solver-level CPU context; modern endpoint taxonomy absent
studies.method_specific_optimizations: FV nonuniform meshes permitted; FD uniform-grid cost advantage discussed
studies.reported_result: Uniform-grid FD may be cheaper, while nonuniform FV can offset per-cell cost by reaching a result with fewer cells and less memory.
studies.limitations: Not a controlled multidimensional GPU study and not a universal comparison.
studies.memory: discussed qualitatively, not recorded as a modern measured endpoint

studies.title: On the Order of Accuracy and Numerical Performance of Two Classes of Finite Volume WENO Schemes
taxonomy_endpoints: genuinely high-order multidimensional FV reconstruction (Class B)
studies.equations_dimensions_grid: linear and nonlinear systems; two-dimensional Cartesian meshes; smooth and shocked solutions
studies.reconstruction_flux: two FV constructions using comparable building blocks
studies.time_integration: reported in paper; not an FD/FV matched variable
studies.hardware_precision: historical CPU timing; precision not a highlighted comparison dimension
studies.comparison_basis: same building blocks and meshes; formal order, shock resolution, and CPU time
studies.correctness: analysis plus smooth and shocked numerical experiments
studies.method_specific_optimizations: Class A is deliberately cheaper/easier; Class B preserves formal multidimensional order
studies.reported_result: Class A is only second order for nonlinear systems while Class B is high order; Class A costs less, and shock resolution can remain comparable on the same mesh despite formal-order differences.
studies.limitations: This is FV-versus-FV, but it proves that an undifferentiated FV label is inadequate for a fair FD/FV comparison.

studies.title: Comparison of Fifth-Order WENO Scheme and Finite Volume WENO-Gas-Kinetic Scheme for Inviscid and Viscous Flow Simulation
studies.weno_family_orders: fifth-order WENO reconstruction in both solvers
studies.equations_dimensions_grid: two-dimensional Euler and Navier-Stokes tests including cavity flow
studies.state_semantics: FD characteristic flux reconstruction versus FV conservative-variable reconstruction
studies.reconstruction_flux: FD uses Steger-Warming flux splitting; FV uses a gas-kinetic flux, so flux physics is intentionally not matched
studies.time_integration: FD uses three-stage Runge-Kutta; FV gas-kinetic evolution differs
studies.hardware_precision: CPU; precision and complete reproducibility environment not reported for modern reuse
studies.comparison_basis: same nominal WENO reconstruction and grids, but intentionally different flux functions and update constructions
studies.execution_boundary: per-step CPU times reported for selected cases
studies.method_specific_optimizations: each method retains its native flux construction
studies.reported_result: The FD solver is about four times faster per step in a reported 2-D cavity case, while the FV gas-kinetic solver can be more accurate and robust on under-resolved viscous flows.
studies.limitations: Not a pure FD/FV ablation: reconstruction variables, flux, and time evolution differ materially.

studies.title: Curvilinear Grids for WENO Methods in Astrophysical Simulations
taxonomy_endpoints: classical finite-difference WENO on mapped grids
studies.weno_family_orders: WENO methods used by the Antares astrophysical solver
studies.equations_dimensions_grid: hydrodynamics; two-dimensional Cartesian and smooth/nonsmooth mapped grids; low- and high-Mach tests
studies.state_semantics: FD pointwise and FV cell-average formulations
studies.time_integration: not isolated as the comparison variable
studies.hardware_precision: CPU; not a modern accelerator comparison
studies.comparison_basis: accuracy/convergence under grid mapping and Mach regime
studies.execution_boundary: performance is not the primary controlled endpoint
studies.reported_result: In the tested mapped-grid setting FD works for high-Mach flow and smooth mappings, while FV remains accurate for low-Mach tests and nonsmooth grids.
studies.limitations: Capability result for one solver/formulation family; it does not imply FV superiority on structured Cartesian grids.

studies.title: Efficient Alternative Finite Difference WENO Schemes for Hyperbolic Conservation Laws
studies.equations_dimensions_grid: hyperbolic conservation laws and systems; structured multidimensional grids
studies.state_semantics: pointwise zone-centered variables with face interpolation and flux-derivative corrections
studies.reconstruction_flux: WENO interpolation, Riemann solvers, and high-order flux-derivative corrections
studies.implementation: low-level scientific implementation plus computer-algebra support
studies.comparison_basis: method construction and qualification, not a complete FD/FV bakeoff
studies.correctness: accuracy and shock tests through high order
studies.method_specific_optimizations: AFD avoids some multidimensional FV reconstruction/quadrature work while retaining Riemann solvers
studies.reported_result: Establishes AFD as a distinct comparator that cannot be conflated with classical split-flux FD.
studies.limitations: No modern differentiable CPU/GPU accuracy-to-time FD/FV matrix.

studies.title: An Alternative Finite Difference WENO-Like Scheme with Physical Constraint Preservation for Divergence-Preserving Hyperbolic Systems
studies.weno_family_orders: third- and fifth-order timed; accuracy demonstrated through ninth order
studies.equations_dimensions_grid: CED, MHD, and RMHD; 2-D 400^2 and 3-D 128^3 structured grids in timing comparison
studies.state_semantics: AFD zone-centered point values plus face-centered constrained fields versus FV zone averages plus face-centered constrained fields
studies.reconstruction_flux: same SSP-RK and authors state identical algorithmic elements where possible; multidimensional Riemann stabilization retained
studies.time_integration: same SSP Runge-Kutta family for the reported AFD/FV timing comparison
studies.hardware_precision: Intel Xeon Gold 6248R; precision not identified as an experimental factor in the comparison section
studies.comparison_basis: same grid zones and problem class; component-matched to the degree allowed by the methods
studies.execution_boundary: CPU solver timing for multidimensional tests
studies.correctness: formal accuracy and stringent CED/MHD/RMHD tests, including physical-constraint preservation
studies.method_specific_optimizations: authors explicitly note that FV Riemann-call reductions were not used and that ADER could improve FV
studies.reported_result: Reported AFD speedups are approximately 7-14x in 2-D and 5-12x in 3-D for the stated CPU cases, depending on order/problem.
studies.limitations: Strong direct evidence but narrow: single-core CPU, divergence-preserving systems, same-grid rather than accuracy-to-time, and a non-fully-optimized FV comparator by author admission.
studies.memory: not reported as a comparison endpoint

studies.title: Cost-Efficient Finite-Volume High-Order Schemes for Compressible Magnetohydrodynamics
studies.weno_family_orders: high-order WENO-based FV through order ten; arbitrarily high-order construction discussed
studies.equations_dimensions_grid: three-dimensional compressible MHD on Cartesian grids with constrained transport
studies.state_semantics: cell and face averages with average-to-point transformations
studies.reconstruction_flux: one reconstruction and two evaluations per dimension with Taylor-expansion transformations; comparator FV uses quadrature; ADER discussed
studies.time_integration: Runge-Kutta versus single-step ADER differences are explicit
studies.hardware_precision: reported in paper; not used here as a direct GradFlow endpoint
studies.comparison_basis: asymptotic and measured cost among FV variants
studies.method_specific_optimizations: central subject of the paper; efficient FV reduces reconstruction/quadrature growth
studies.reported_result: Best-practical FV can remove much of the cost assumed by a standard tensor-product quadrature implementation; FV implementation choice is therefore a mandatory benchmark variable.
studies.limitations: No direct classical-FD comparator and no differentiable PyTorch head-to-head.

studies.title: JAX-Fluids 2.0: Towards HPC for Differentiable CFD of Compressible Two-Phase Flows
taxonomy_endpoints: component and characteristic flux-splitting paths with FD-like algebra
studies.weno_family_orders: multiple hard-coded WENO orders and variants
studies.equations_dimensions_grid: compressible single- and two-phase flows; structured Cartesian; multi-dimensional and multi-accelerator
studies.state_semantics: primarily finite-volume cell states; flux-splitting paths require exact classification per experiment
studies.reconstruction_flux: multiple reconstruction variables, Riemann solvers, and flux-splitting choices
studies.comparison_basis: production capability and scaling, not a controlled FD/FV comparison
studies.reported_result: Shows that differentiable accelerator WENO CFD is established prior art; use of FV is not evidence of universal FV superiority.
studies.limitations: No matched FD/FV accuracy-to-time or gradient comparison.
studies.memory: distributed capability reported; matched FD/FV memory absent

studies.title: HOPE: An Arbitrary-Order Non-Oscillatory Finite-Volume Shallow Water Dynamical Core with Automatic Differentiation
studies.weno_family_orders: arbitrary-order WENO-Z; experiments through order thirteen
studies.equations_dimensions_grid: two-dimensional shallow-water equations on spherical/structured geometry
studies.state_semantics: cell-average finite volume with multidimensional polynomial reconstruction and face quadrature
studies.reconstruction_flux: tensor-product polynomial reconstruction, Gaussian quadrature, and Riemann fluxes
studies.hardware_precision: CPU/GPU PyTorch; selected float32 performance observations
studies.comparison_basis: FV capability, order, differentiation, and implementation variants; no FD comparator
studies.execution_boundary: simulation and operator observations; not a frozen FD/FV endpoint
studies.method_specific_optimizations: PyTorch tensor representations compared inside the FV code
studies.reported_result: Establishes arbitrary-order differentiable PyTorch FV-WENO prior art and a credible close-system comparator family.
studies.limitations: Different equations, geometry, WENO variant, and no controlled FD endpoint.

studies.title: GPU Driven Finite Difference WENO Scheme for Real Time Solution of the Shallow Water Equations
studies.weno_family_orders: PIF-WENO-type scheme; third order in space and second order in time in the reported shallow-water implementation
studies.equations_dimensions_grid: multidimensional hyperbolic conservation laws on structured grids
studies.time_integration: Picard-integral formulation reduces conventional RK staging
studies.hardware_precision: GPU and CPU performance reported in primary paper
studies.comparison_basis: GPU acceleration of FD WENO, not FD versus FV
studies.reported_result: Confirms that GPU FD-WENO is established and can be efficient.
studies.limitations: Cannot answer comparative FD/FV efficiency or differentiability.

studies.title: GPU-Accelerated DNS of Compressible Turbulent Flows
studies.equations_dimensions_grid: three-dimensional compressible Navier-Stokes DNS on structured grids
studies.hardware_precision: GPU and CPU systems reported in paper
studies.comparison_basis: GPU FD optimization and alternatives, not controlled FD versus FV
studies.reported_result: Provides a native-GPU FD performance precedent and prevents any claim that GPU FD-WENO is new.
studies.limitations: No matched FV comparator, ordinary-PyTorch path, or differentiation comparison.
studies.memory: GPU memory strategy discussed; no FD/FV accuracy-to-memory comparison
